name: Beans
description: Beans represent a highly concentrated, non-animal proteinaceous and carbohydrate phytomatrix belonging to the Fabaceae family (Phaseolus vulgaris), characterized by an intricate network of globular storage proteins (phaseolin), low-glycemic alpha-linked glucan polymers (amylose), and a dense matrix of non-digestible structural non-starch polysaccharides. Operating as a critical regulatory therapeutic food, this botanical repository drives systematic blood glucose attenuation, optimizes peripheral insulin sensitivity through delayed upper-intestinal transit, and delivers structural building blocks for lean tissue synthesis. Furthermore, the matrix isolates high concentrations of divalent mineral cofactors and heterocyclic polyphenolic structures that possess potent radical-scavenging and vascular endothelial lining protection capacities.
macroIntro: The macronutrient profile of cooked beans exhibits an exceptional thermodynamic and nutritional density, presenting a balanced delivery of premium plant peptides alongside slow-hydrolyzing complex polyglucans that yield extended cellular satiety.
microIntro: A major physiological repository of fundamental metallic cofactors, water-soluble B-complex vitamins, and macro-elements required for genomic stability, red blood cell synthesis, and neuromuscular tone.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: An efficient and sustained metabolic energy output derived entirely from low-glycemic, slow-cleaving complex starches.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: A rich plant-based nitrogenous input composed of globulin and albumin fractions, valuable for myofibrillar repair and cellular maintenance.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: A negligible lipid presence, consisting mostly of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids built into the remaining cellular membranes.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Dominated by high-molecular amylose starches that undergo gradual, non-insulinogenic enzymatic digestion in the intestinal lumen.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: An essential transition metal necessary for red blood cell hemoglobin synthesis, functional myoglobin coordination, and cytochrome activity.

microNutrients.name: Folate (B9)
microNutrients.description: A fundamental organic coenzyme crucial for single-carbon methyl transfer cycles, direct nucleotide biosynthesis, and erythrocyte maturation.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A dense combination of soluble pectins and insoluble celluloses that optimize intestinal motility and bind bile acids to assist clearance.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A vital intracellular electrolyte that drives vascular smooth muscle hyperpolarization, promoting healthy blood pressure regulation.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: An indispensable alkaline earth metal cofactor for over 300 enzymatic reactions, regulating ATP utilization and neuromuscular transmission.

healthBenefits: Glycemic Instability Attenuation and Insulin Sensitivity: The dense layout of structural amylose and soluble viscous fibers slows down upper-intestinal glucose absorption, reducing postprandial insulin surges and optimizing long-term peripheral receptor sensitivity.

Bile Acid Sequestration and Hypocholesterolemic Effects: Soluble fiber complexes create a viscous gel in the intestinal lumen that physically traps bile acids, forcing the liver to deplete systemic circulating low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol to synthesize new bile.

Short-Chain Fatty Acid Generation and Microbiome Prebiosis: Non-digestible oligosaccharides and resistant starches travel to the large bowel to serve as fermentable fuel for commensal microflora, accelerating the production of cytoprotective butyrate and acetate.

Endothelial Compliance and Blood Pressure Modulation: The substantial concentration of potassium and magnesium relaxes vascular smooth muscle architecture, downregulating peripheral resistance and relieving structural stress across the arterial wall.
precautionsIntro: Due to the presence of intense defense proteins and complex sugars within the legume seed, beans require strict dietary preparation and clinical monitoring:
precautions: Phytohemagglutinin Lectin and Phytate Antinutritional Toxicity: Raw or undercooked beans express dangerous levels of phytohemagglutinin (lectin), which binds intestinal epithelial cell linings to cause severe enterocyte disruption and malabsorption; extended soaking and boiling are required for thermal denaturation.

Oligosaccharide-Induced Colonic Fermentation: High native amounts of alpha-galactosides (raffinose and stachyose) cannot be broken down by human digestive enzymes, moving into the large bowel where anaerobic bacteria generate significant carbon dioxide, hydrogen, and methane gases.

Purine Overload in Metabolic Hyperuricemia: The cellular matrix contains a moderate amount of purine bases whose downstream catabolic pathway increases serum uric acid concentrations, creating a clear risk of needle-like crystal precipitation in patients with active gouty arthritis.
